source_title: Joshimath Chopper Crash: Chopper With Six Onboard Crashes in Uttarakhand, Search Underway - India Today - India Today
source_excerpt:
A Trans Bharat helicopter carrying six people, including the pilot and five passengers, crashed near Chhai village behind Hathi Pahad in Joshimath while en route from Badrinath to Fata. The aircraft took off around 1:30 PM before losing contact. Local residents reported sighting smoke and hearing loud sounds from the valley, alerting the Indian Army Signal Unit and Chamoli district administration. Rescue teams comprising the State Disaster Response Force, Indian Army, Indo-Tibetan Border Police, and local police have been deployed, alongside two Army Signal Unit helicopters. Adverse weather, heavy rainfall, snowfall, and dense cloud cover have severely hampered efforts to trace the wreckage. Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami confirmed that he is closely monitoring the situation and directed authorities to immediately airlift any critically injured persons to medical centres. This incident marks the third helicopter emergency in the Char Dham region during October. Read More

PM Modi Slams Opposition on Rumours Amid Kharge Slogan Row, JP Nadda Hits Out
Addressing a gathering in Gujarat, Prime Minister Narendra Modi criticised the opposition for allegedly spreading fake news and panic regarding urea and gas supplies during geopolitical tensions in the Gulf region. He stated that his government ensured farmers received fertiliser at lower prices despite global crises, accusing rivals of attempting to create chaos to malign him. Meanwhile, political tensions escalated over Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge's controversial remarks made during an event in Bihar, which followed crowd chants stating that the Prime Minister would not go anywhere. Reacting to Kharge's statements at the Health Wealth Summit, Union Minister JP Nadda strongly condemned the Congress leadership, terming the remarks as reflecting mental bankruptcy and arguing that the opposition's conduct has become laughable.
CEC Mock Impeachment Postponed Due to Rain; INDIA Bloc Plans Ramlila Maidan March
The INDIA bloc has postponed its public mock impeachment of the Chief Election Commissioner due to adverse weather conditions in the national capital. The event, titled Jan Maha Abhiyog, was scheduled to be held at Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge's residence at 10 Rajaji Marg before rain affected the open-air venue arrangements. Opposition leaders announced that the deferred event will now take place tomorrow at 3 PM. Addressing the media, leaders highlighted opposition solidarity across multiple regional parties and appealed to students, youth, workers, and civil society to join their ongoing demonstrations. They alleged widespread election manipulation and accused the government of undermining constitutional processes and democracy. Leaders also confirmed that a joint march to Ramlila Maidan will proceed as scheduled on 1 November, with senior alliance leaders participating. Channel reporter Shivani Sharma noted that while the mock impeachment holds no legal or legislative binding, the symbolic drive aims to mount political pressure on the government.
Election Commission Row: Amit Shah Challenges Rahul Gandhi and Akhilesh Yadav to Debate in House
Union Home Minister Amit Shah launched a sharp attack against Congress leader Rahul Gandhi and Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav, daring them to debate issues regarding the Election Commission inside a special session of Parliament rather than taking to the streets. Addressing party workers in Uttar Pradesh, Shah noted that Rahul Gandhi remains fixated on the 2024 general election outcomes despite the National Democratic Alliance governing across 22 states. He asserted that the Bharatiya Janata Party's foothold in Uttar Pradesh remains unshakeable and highlighted the end of mafia raj under Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath alongside the construction of the Ram Mandir. The Home Minister further criticised past appeasement politics under the Samajwadi Party administration and dismissed opposition rallies against democratic institutions following the recent Legislative Council election results. Motivating booth-level cadre for the upcoming 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly polls, Shah expressed confidence that the party would secure a full majority victory.
Choosing Diagnostic Labs, Cheap Packages & Predictive Tests
At the Healthtech Summit, diagnostic experts and medical leaders examined criteria for selecting pathology laboratories and utilizing modern diagnostic tools. The panel addressed risks associated with commercial testing packages and misleading marketing, urging patients to prioritize laboratory accreditation, physician supervision, quality control, and clinical history. Panellists evaluated screenings for lifestyle diseases including diabetes and cardiovascular conditions, while addressing the clinical impacts of over-testing and missed diagnoses. The summit also explored predictive medicine, whole-body imaging, gut microbiome profiling, genetic sequencing, and coronary calcium scoring for disease risk stratification. Medical practitioners emphasized the requirement for clinical guidance and pre-test counselling for advanced procedures. Addressing antimicrobial resistance, the panel called for replacing outdated diagnostics, such as the Widal test for typhoid, with targeted methodologies to reduce unnecessary antibiotic prescriptions. Additionally, the discussions covered the application of artificial intelligence in radiology and pathology, outlining how clinical algorithms serve as precision decision-support tools alongside specialist physicians.
